Sablé Cookies

Named after the French town of Sablé-sur-Sarthe, these buttery shortbread cookies are a cornerstone of French patisserie. The word "sablé" means "sand" in French — a nod to the delicate, crumbly texture that melts in your mouth. Simple ingredients, perfected technique.

Cookie France Sweet Easy

The Sandy Secret

The distinctive texture comes from the sheer proportion of butter to flour, and from egg yolks instead of whole eggs. No water means no gluten development — which is exactly what gives the finished cookie its crumbly, melt-in-your-mouth bite.

The Recipe

Yield 24–30 cookies
Prep Time 20 minutes
Baking Time 12–15 minutes
Total Time 1 hr 40 min

What you'll need

  • Mixing bowl
  • Hand or stand mixer
  • Baking sheet
  • Parchment paper
  • Pastry brush
  • Sharp knife

Ingredients

  • 225g (1 cup) unsalted butter, softened
  • 150g (1¼ cups) confectioners' sugar
  • 2 egg yolks (whites reserved for the edges)
  • 1 tsp vanilla extract
  • 300g (2½ cups) all-purpose flour
  • ¼ tsp salt
  • Zest of 1 lemon or orange (optional)
  • Coarse or turbinado sugar, for the edges

Instructions

  1. Preparation Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
  2. Mix the dough Cream softened butter and sugar on medium speed until light and fluffy. Add egg yolks and vanilla, mixing until incorporated. Add optional citrus zest. Sift in flour and salt, mixing on low speed just until the dough comes together.
  3. Chill Divide the dough in two and roll each half into a log about 4cm (1½ inches) across. Wrap and refrigerate for at least 1 hour, until firm.
  4. Sugar the edges Lightly beat the reserved egg whites. Brush each chilled log all over with egg white, then roll it in coarse sugar to coat — this becomes the crackly rim on every slice.
  5. Slice Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F). Slice the logs into rounds about 1cm (⅜ inch) thick and arrange 2cm apart on the prepared baking sheet.
  6. Bake Bake for 12–15 minutes until the edges just begin to turn golden. Cool on the sheet for 2 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack.

Tips & Notes

  • Chill the sliced cookies on the baking sheet for 15 minutes before baking for cleaner edges
  • The logs keep well — refrigerate up to 3 days or freeze up to a month, and slice straight from cold
  • For plain sablés, skip the egg-white-and-sugar step and slice the logs as they are
  • Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to one week
